english_verification.review_scope: Read the complete H84 source body and original evidence page; checked the current H84 country history, special election government reform, native English Glozok and mithril narrative, and the actual Freegobbin event text. Read the complete supporting Wiki Markdown chunk. No full mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The 1428 liberation account and later mithril-production detail come from Wiki revision 28122; they are not established as completed 1444 conditions by the H84 country-history file.

Source conflict: the original Chinese gameplay rationale says the current version lacks evidence for large-scale atrocities, while current English event mountainshark_events.27.d explicitly describes mass killings, destruction of homes and relatives, and erasure of tribal records and culture. The translation preserves both source claims and does not change Chinese text or scores.

rationale.colonization: There is some need to expand into underground empty holds.
rationale.complexity: Political institutions, industry, and multi-stage wars are intertwined.
rationale.dark_story: Anti-slavery ideals coexist with brutal revenge.
rationale.difficulty: Requires building momentum from a high-pressure start; not tested in an actual playthrough.
rationale.diplomacy: Mountain integration is present but is not the main focus.
rationale.early_pressure: A small clan faces powerful neighbors in the mountains.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Engineering and mithril technology are significant; the theme leans toward artifice.
rationale.narrative_density: The founding of a state by escaped slaves and the revenge arc run through the missions.
rationale.tall_play: The mithril industry and clan institutions require long-term development.
rationale.trade_economy: The mithril industry is the economic hallmark.
rationale.warfare: Early land grabs and later wars of revenge are prominent.

identity.appearance: A goblin clan already present in 1444.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: There was once a time where goblins roamed the Serpentspine freely, without anyone to oppress them. Many clans struggled against dwarves and orcs, but none other had to endure the pain we had been subjected to. As slaves to a black orc warband we were the lowest of the low, we were worth less than the dirt we slept on. But deep in our hearts there stirred a thought. A faint memory of hope that someday we could be free once more. This hope nurtured us, strengthened our resolve. It is only through these decades of hidden resistance that we could eventually gain our freedom from the orcs.

description.text: The rise of Dookanson meant that almost all orc warbands had left the Serpentspine, leaving behind a gigantic power vacuum that is slowly being filled by the innumerous goblins crawling out of the eternal shadow. If we want to stay relevant in this world we must make haste and fill these empty halls with our own goblin kin who serve us and only us.

description.text: To survive in the harsh world of the Serpentspine the Clanboss needs only the most capable advisors around him. But in a world forged by fearsome strife and bloody battles such as the Serpentspine a simple academic is useless if they can’t fight. To prove that an advisor can survive the world they need to fight for their place. Whoever wishes to lead must defeat the one in front of him. This way only the truly strong will be the ones to advise the Clanboss on matters of state.

description.text: The brutal advisors of our clan demand high pay for their services which has put significant financial strain on our treasuries. To ease the burden we have supplemented their pay with coins not made of gold but of mithril, which we have in relative abundance thanks to our home, the mithril hold of Mithradhûm. This mithril coinage enables us to put our gold to other use.

description.text: Left in the wake of the fall of Aul-Dwarov many holds and roads are full of ancient dwarven mechanisms and machinery of war. Those that have not been trashed by roaming black orc warbands can still be put to some use. Especially the old cannons and firearms are useful once they are outfitted and repaired with what we can find elsewhere. These patchwork weapons are quite hefty and to our delight we have found that they leave more than a few scars and blue spots.

description.text: While drills and pickaxes are perfectly suitable tools to scratch the rock of the Serpentspine they are not much use if we want to dig down fast. For that we need to blast away all of the useless rock by firing explosives from our mithril-cannons and free the precious, shiny metals, obliterating the surrounding stone in much the same way as we did to our warband when we gained freedom. These new mining practices will show the world what it truly means to dig a mine.

description.text: Our clan’s name comes from Glozok the Shark, the goblin who brought us out of slavery and into freedom. Under his leadership we have become more than a ragtag group of warriors. To this day it is his fierce wisdom that guides us and our Clanboss into the future. Each goblin of Mountainshark tries to emulate the genius, the cunning, and the incredible violence which he showed us.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players expecting a wholly positive liberator story or disliking a high-pressure start in the mountains.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Seize land to survive, shelter escaped slaves, then use mithril and political reform to support expansion; decide conditionally whether to form I98.
player_overview.overview: Mountainshark begins as a goblin community that escaped slavery around 1428. In 1444 it remains a small clan, but has its own Glozok-inspired leadership tradition, mithril-industry ambitions, and strong anti-slavery cause. Its missions shelter escapees and incorporate different groups, while also depicting the dark revenge of massacring former slaveholders and erasing their culture. It may later form the Allclan, but that is a separate entry.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy goblin industry, elective politics, and a complex revenge narrative.
signature_features: A goblin clan founded by former slaves, with Glozok-inspired elections.
Mithril production and mountain engineering create an industrial path.
A story where liberation, inclusion, and brutal revenge coexist.
player_overview.tagline: Escaped goblins form a new clan and fight for a future in the mountains through elections, mithril industry, and revenge.

reasons: A rare story of goblin state-building by escaped slaves.
Mithril industry and political reform go hand in hand.
warnings: The text explicitly depicts violent revenge.
I98's missions and reforms are assessed separately after formation.

values.rationale: Sheltering escaped slaves and including different groups are concrete positive evidence; the narrative of massacring slaveholders and erasing their culture is a substantial negative. Warfare itself is not penalized.
red_flags: An event explicitly depicts the massacre of slaveholders.
The revenge narrative calls for erasing their cultural memory.
